newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower on lack of follow through.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower on lack of follow through.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled lower amid a lack of follow-through fund buying and on an increase in hedging tied to fresh country selling, traders said.
KCBT wheat rallied early on limited fund buying, but weakened as the March contract failed to hold on above resistance at $4.25. The last time March traded above $4.25 was Dec 18, 1996, traders said.
Traders said strong follow-through buying failed to materialize amid feelings that Wednesday's USDA supply and demand report was not all that bullish for wheat.
"This day was characterized by disappointing price action," a trader said. "Part of that was because we did not receive anything positive off the (USDA's) all-wheat supply and demand tables."
Overnight news from East Asia also appeared to dismiss speculation that short-term U.S. wheat export prospects might get a boost because of Canadian grain shipment problems.
KCBT wheat settled 1/2 to 2-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with March down 2-3/4 cents at $4.20-3/4.
Traders said Rosenthal Collins, E D & F Man International and Cargill Investor Services were among the early buyers.
